Detect variable roles heuristically

Source: R/roles.R
sd_detect_roles.Rd

Guesses a role for each variable in an sd_data object, based on simple rules (data type, value range, name pattern, cardinality). This is a heuristic starting point, not a guarantee — always check the result and correct individual variables with sd_set_role() where the guess is wrong.

Usage

sd_detect_roles(x)

Arguments

x

An sd_data object.

Value

The same sd_data object, with meta$roles filled in.

Details

Roles used elsewhere in the package: "id", "likert", "nominal", "continuous", "date", "text", "weight", "unknown".

The heuristic, checked in this order for each variable:

date

Column class is Date, POSIXct or POSIXt.

id

Variable name matches id/tunnus (whole word or suffix, e.g. vastaaja_id), OR every non-missing value is unique and there are more than 10 respondents.

weight

Variable name matches paino/weight/wt and the variable is numeric.

likert

Numeric, whole-number values, 2–11 distinct values, and a value range of 10 or less. This is a common shape for Likert/ordinal scales, but it also matches other small-range counts (e.g. number of children) — check the result.

continuous

Any other numeric variable.

text

Character/factor where more than half the values are unique, or the average value length is over 30 characters — a proxy for open-ended text.

nominal

Any other character, factor, or logical variable.

unknown

Anything not covered above.

Recommended order

Run sd_set_missing() before sd_detect_roles() whenever your data uses sentinel missing-value codes (e.g. 99, -9). Otherwise a sentinel code widens a variable's apparent value range — a 1–5 Likert item with a handful of 99s looks like it ranges from 1 to 99, and gets classified as "continuous" instead of "likert".

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
aineisto <- sd_read("survey_data.csv")
aineisto <- sd_detect_roles(aineisto)
print(aineisto)
} # }
